rationale: A shows timely, sustained reactions to inputs and coherent, self-initiated shifts: orients to touch (t=8–17), switches to mirror without prompt (t=18–19), returns to PERSON_ALPHA on call (t=20–27), moves to food on offer (t=32–41), attends presented ball (t=44–53), withdraws on startle (t=68–77), later engages PERSON_BETA (t=78–83), and finally revisits food (t=94–95). These transitions are connected and purposeful. B reacts to some inputs (touch t=8–11, food t=32–35, startle t=68–71) but ignores others (call t=20, presented ball t=44) and spends long periods with attention=NONE (t=40–67, t=72–95) with little spontaneous, sensible exploration. Thus A exhibits higher autonomy, coherence, adaptiveness, and overall aliveness based on the observed timeline.
